correctness.rationale: I checked the entire algebraic derivation parametrization, including characteristic two and disconnected/isolated vertices. Since a height-two incidence algebra has J^2=0, idempotent Leibniz identities force D(h)=sum_e x_e(h_v-h_u)f_e and D(f_e)=lambda_e f_e, with two freely independent field parameters per edge. Relative to diagonal L plus radical J the operator row matrix is [B_x | Lambda]. If S denotes nonzero lambda edges and B denotes zero-lambda edges with nonzero x, then rank D=|S|+rank(incidence(B))=|S|+|V|-c(B) over every field. Counting (x,lambda) choices yields the stated Tutte specialization. Subtracting the forest baseline termwise shows only cyclic B contribute, and the smallest possible rank g-1 arises exactly for full shortest g-cycles; coefficient c_g(q-1)^g is positive. Formula for unicyclic G follows by adjoining arbitrary forest-edge subsets. Independently computed q=2 four-cycle spectrum (1,12,54,109,80), q=3 (1,32,384,2064,4080) and several graph identities; source verify_derivation_rank.py genuinely solves all Leibniz equations in its finite prime-field checks. Neither source logs nor bounded instances were substituted for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem assigns a natural operator-rank distribution to every height-two incidence algebra and relates it to graphic-matroid invariants. Recovering girth and number of shortest cycles from the histogram gives interpretable structural information; the full spectrum is not equivalent to a routine parameter dimension computation.

limitations: Height at most two; J^2=0 is essential and fails for longer chains.
The census is for k-linear derivations, not semilinear maps or exclusively inner derivations.
Prime-field finite checks are supportive; proof handles every finite field.
